Interface LogProperties

All Known Subinterfaces:
LogProperties.Listable, LogProperties.MutableLogProperties
All Known Implementing Classes:
ForwardingLogProperties, LogProperties.AbstractNested, LogProperties.StandardProperties
public interface LogProperties
Provides String based properties like System.getProperty(String) for default configuration of logging levels and output. Since Rainbow Gum is configuration agnostic LogProperties is a simple string key and string value interface to allow almost any configuration implementation. The only required method to implement is valueOrNull(String) and thus LogProperties is a functional like interface but using builder() is preferred so that a description can be added.

If a custom LogProperties is not configured the default RainbowGum uses System properties.

The built-in properties to configure RainbowGum are modeled after Spring Boot logging

LogProperties should generally be accessed with forKey(String) (see LogProperty) which will allow safe programmatic data conversion of the flat key values and useful error messages to users if the property cannot be mapped or is missing. For more declarative injection of properties see LogConfigurable which will generate builders that can use LogProperties.

Rainbow Gum treats "." in the keys as special separator analogous to JavaScript/JSON and various other configuration systems. Furthermore to work with a wide set of configuration systems once a property key has a value it is RECOMMENDED that there should not be other property key value with a key that is a prefix of the previously mentioned key. For example allowing two properties logging.example=stuff, logging.example.a=A is not recommended as logging.example is defined as a leaf. The exception to this rule is keys that end with a logger name, such as levels, for consistency with Spring Boot. LogProperties.AbstractNested is one way for a nested format to read them.

Rainbow Gum out of the the box supports parsing two formats into properties: Properties text, and URI.getRawQuery() percent encoded query parameters. The two different formats have different behavior for listOrNull(String) and mapOrNull(String). If a custom format of LogProperties is created those two methods may need to be extended.

A convention used through out Rainbow Gum is to have the property names as constants as it makes documentation easier. These constants name are suffixed with _PROPERTY or _PREFIX the former being a fully qualified key that maybe parameterized and the latter being a partial key ending with ".". The fully qualified keys are like leaves on a tree.

Property keys can be parameterized by using interpolateKey(String, Map) and a general pattern is logging.component.{name}.prop where "name" is a parameter. Many property constants use this to allow multiple configuration of components by name.

Built-in Property Patterns
Property Pattern Description
"logging.level" + "." + logger = LEVEL Sets the level for the logger. If logger name is missing or is root then it is considered the root logger. System.Logger.Level.INFO is the default level for the root logger.
"logging.change.mode" = LogConfig.ChangePublisher.ChangeMode Whether runtime changes are on for the configuration. Default is LogConfig.ChangePublisher.ChangeMode.OFF. When on, the loggers that may change are chosen with "logging.change.logger".
"logging.change.logger" + "." + logger = boolean | List<LogConfig.ChangePublisher.ChangeType> What may change at runtime for the logger and its children. By design RainbowGum does not allow loggers to change levels once initialized. Default is none. Has no effect unless "logging.change.mode" is on.
"logging.routes" = List<String> A comma separated list of routes that should be enabled. If not set "default" is the default.
"logging.route.{name}.appenders" = List<String> A comma separated list of appenders associated with the route. If not set "logging.appenders" is used.
"logging.route.{name}.filters" = List<String> A comma separated list of filters applied in order to the route's events. Default is none.
"logging.route.{name}.filter.{filter}." + propertyName Configures a filter listed in "logging.route.{name}.filters", where filter is the name it is listed with, for example logging.route.default.filter.throttle.rate.
"logging.route.{name}.publisher.uri" = URI Looks up a publisher by URI scheme using the LogPublisherRegistry. The publisher is then configured by the other properties starting with "logging.route.{name}.publisher.".
"logging.route.{name}.publisher." + scheme + . + propertyName Configures the route's publisher of the type selected by the URI scheme, for example logging.route.default.publisher.async.bufferSize. The scheme is the one written in the URI, so async settings apply to whichever publisher is registered as async.
"logging.appenders" = List<String> A comma separated list of appenders that should be enabled. If not set "console" is the default.
"logging.appender.{name}.output.uri" = URI Looks up an output by URI scheme using the LogOutputRegistry. The output is then configured by the other properties starting with "logging.appender.{name}.output.".
"logging.appender.{name}.encoder.uri" = URI Looks up an encoder by URI scheme using the LogEncoderRegistry. The encoder is then configured by the other properties starting with "logging.appender.{name}.encoder.".
"logging.appender.{name}.output." + scheme + . + propertyName Configures the appender's output of the type selected by the URI scheme, for example logging.appender.file.output.file.bufferSize. An output built without an appender uses its own name in place of the appender's.
"logging.appender.{name}.encoder." + scheme + . + propertyName Configures the appender's encoder of the type selected by the URI scheme, for example logging.appender.console.encoder.json5.keyValues. Each type has its own keys, so switching an appender's encoder leaves the other type's settings unread rather than misread. An encoder built without an appender uses its own name in place of the appender's.
"logging.file.name" = URI A URI or file path to log to a file. This is for Spring Boot compatibility.

    • DEBUG_PROPERTY

      static final String DEBUG_PROPERTY
      Controls direct fail-safe bootstrap diagnostics. OFF (also false) is the default; ERROR dumps on build failure, while INFO also dumps after successful config builds. ALL (also true) additionally prints a LogReporter report after RainbowGum.start() starts the logging components. Read from system properties before properties providers run, so it remains available when loading configuration fails. The system property overrides LogConfig.Builder.debug(LogConfig.DebugModeType).

      Property: logging.debug

      See Also:

      static final String GROUP_PROPERTY
      Group property with list of logger names. The level of the group is set with "logging.level" + .{name} = Level or on the router itself with "logging.route.{name}.level" + .{name} = Level. The group name can also be used in place of a logger name with "logging.change.logger" and "logging.caller.logger". This is largely compatible with Spring Boot Log Groups .

    • GLOBAL_SHUTDOWN_HOOK_PROPERTY

      static final String GLOBAL_SHUTDOWN_HOOK_PROPERTY
      Whether starting the global Rainbow Gum registers a JVM shutdown hook that closes it: on (the default) or off, with true and false as aliases. Set it to off when the application or framework closes Rainbow Gum itself as the last step of its own shutdown: JVM shutdown hooks run concurrently in no set order, so events logged by other hooks after this one has run are lost, except errors, which are echoed to standard error. In code, see LogConfig.Builder.shutdownHook(LogConfig.Globals.ShutdownHookMode).

      Property: logging.global.shutdownHook

    • GLOBAL_OPTIMIZE_PROPERTY

      static final String GLOBAL_OPTIMIZE_PROPERTY
      Opts every appender/encoder that has not been given an explicit choice into whatever this release currently believes is the best buffering/locking strategy for the platform the process is actually running on, instead of the fixed defaults (LogAppender.AppenderType.LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER, a CharsetEncoder-based encode) used otherwise. An explicit choice - programmatic (appenderType(...), useGetBytes(...)) or via a more specific property (LogAppender.APPENDER_TYPE_PROPERTY) - always wins over this property; it only ever fills in what would otherwise be unset.

      What "best" resolves to today, and why that is not a contract: currently this only has an effect under GraalVM native-image (detected the same way LogAppender.AppenderType.AUTO_DETECT is - see its javadoc), where it sets the default appender type to AUTO_DETECT (this benchmark's own measurements found SYNCHRONIZED_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER a real, repeatable win over the plain-JVM default there) and defaults text encoders to String.getBytes(Charset)-based encoding over the default CharsetEncoder-based one. On a plain JVM this property currently changes nothing at all - the measurements that motivated the native-image behavior above pointed the other way on HotSpot. None of this is a promise: as this project benchmarks more platforms, JDK versions, and encode strategies, what "optimize" resolves to on a given platform - including whether it does anything on a plain JVM at all - can and will change between releases without notice. Pin an explicit appender type/encoder strategy instead if a deployment needs a specific one to always be used.

      Property: logging.global.optimize

      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • MESSAGE_FORMAT_STYLE_PROPERTY

      static final String MESSAGE_FORMAT_STYLE_PROPERTY
      How the java.util.logging, System.Logger and JBoss Logging message style formats a message with arguments, named after the implementation that formats the same way:
      • jdk (default, alias jboss): MessageFormat is used only when the message has an argument index such as {0}, so It's done is logged as is. A Throwable argument is formatted like any other argument.
      • log4j2 (alias logback): MessageFormat is used whenever the message has arguments, so It's done with an argument is logged as Its done, because an apostrophe is a quote. A Throwable that is the last argument is formatted like any other argument and also logged with its stack trace.

      Property: logging.messageformat.style

      See Also:
      • LogMessageFormatter.ofJUL(LogProperties)

    • valueOrNull

    • value

    • listOrNull

      default @Nullable List<String> listOrNull(String key)
      Gets a list or null if the key is missing and by default uses parseList(String). The default implementation will parse the string value as a list using parseList(String) but custom implementations may rely on their own parsing or the data type is built-in to the backing configuration system.

      The default format is a single property value that is comma or ampersand separated and percent-encoded ( application/x-www-form-urlencoded) for entries needing to contain the separator or an equals sign, for example: 

      logging.appenders=console,file
      resolves to ["console", "file"], and: 
      logging.appenders=one%20two,three%2Cfour
      (a space and an escaped comma) resolves to ["one two", "three,four"]. See parseList(String) for empty elements.
      Parameters:
      key - property name.
      Returns:
      list or null.
      API Note
      the reason empty list is not returned for missing key is that it creates ambiguity so null is returned when key is missing.

    • mapOrNull

      default @Nullable Map<String,String> mapOrNull(String key)
      Gets a map or null if the key is missing and by default uses parseMap(String). The default implementation will parse the string value as map using parseMap(String) but custom implementations may rely on their own parsing or the data type is built-in to the backing configuration system.

      The returned map must iterate in a stable order, the same every time for the same configuration, preferably the order its entries were declared.

      The default format is a single property value that is comma or ampersand separated key=value pairs, percent-encoded ( application/x-www-form-urlencoded) for entries needing to contain the separator or an equals sign, for example: 

      logging.appender.console.encoder.gelf.headers=environment=prod,region=us-east
      resolves to {"environment": "prod", "region": "us-east"}, and: 
      logging.appender.console.encoder.gelf.headers=region=us%20east
      (a percent-encoded space) resolves to {"region": "us east"}.

      When that property is not set, the map can instead be given as a list of its keys in key.keys and each value in key.mapKey, which works with sources that only hold flat values such as system properties or environment variables, keeps the declared order, and needs no encoding: 

      logging.appender.console.encoder.gelf.headers.keys=environment,region
logging.appender.console.encoder.gelf.headers.environment=prod
logging.appender.console.encoder.gelf.headers.region=us east
      A key listed without a value is an error.
      Parameters:
      key - property name.
      Returns:
      map or null.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if a key listed in key.keys is empty or has no value.
      API Note
      the reason empty map is not returned for missing key is that it creates ambiguity so null is returned when key is missing.

    • visit

      default <R extends @Nullable Object> @Nullable R visit(String key, BiFunction<LogProperties, String, @Nullable R> visitor)
      Visits this properties with visitor, by default just applying visitor to this and key directly. A composite/aggregate LogProperties (one backed by more than one underlying source) overrides this to recursively visit each of its members in order, returning the first non-null result - which member actually produced it is exactly what visitor is handed as its first argument, so a composite never needs to know anything about what visitor is trying to build (a raw value, a resolved property, or anything else); it just walks its members and stops at the first hit.
      Type Parameters:
      R - result type.
      Parameters:
      key - property key.
      visitor - applied to (the member of this properties that ends up handling the visit, key); a null return means keep visiting.
      Returns:
      first non-null result, or null if nothing visited produced one.

    • parseMultiMap

      static Map<String, List<String>> parseMultiMap(String query)
      Parses a URI query for a multiple value map. The list values of the map maybe empty if the query parameter does not have any values associated with it which would be the case if there is a parameter (key) with no "=" following it. For example the following would have three entries of a,b,c all with empty list: 
      
a&b&c&
      Parameters:

    • parseList

      static List<String> parseList(String query)
      Parses a list of strings from a string that is percent encoded for escaping (application/x-www-form-urlencoded) where the separator can be either "&" or ",".

      An example would be using ampersand: 

       "a&b%20B&c" -> ["a","b B","c"]
      and comma: 
       "a,b,c" -> ["a","b","c"]

      An element may be empty. One empty element at the start and one at the end are dropped, so a value assembled from parts that may be missing still works ("a," and ",a," are ["a"]), while every other empty element is kept: 

       "" -> []
 ",," -> [""]
 "a,,b" -> ["a","","b"]
 "a,," -> ["a",""]
      An equals sign is part of the element: "a=b" is ["a=b"].
      Parameters:
      query - the comma or ampersand delimited string.
      Returns:
      list of strings

    • findUpPathOrNull

      static <T extends @Nullable Object> @Nullable T findUpPathOrNull(String key, Function<String, @Nullable T> resolveFunc)
      Searches a "." separated property path recursing up the path till a non null value (not missing) is found.

      For example assume we have a single property set like logging.level.com.stuff=DEBUG and we call this function with logging.level.com.stuff.a.b.

      1. logging.level.com.stuff.a.b will resolve to null
      2. logging.level.com.stuff.a will resolve to null
      3. logging.level.com.stuff will resolve to "DEBUG", stop and return "DEBUG".
      Type Parameters:
      T - type to return.
      Parameters:
      key - the initial path.
      resolveFunc - function that returns the value at path or null.
      Returns:
      value or null if no non null value can be found.

    • interpolateKey

      static String interpolateKey(String key, Function<String, ? extends @Nullable String> lookup) throws IllegalArgumentException
      Replaces property key parameters by using the lookup function. Property keys are often parameterized usually by some name. The parameters are surrounded by curly braces and replaced by the lookup function. An example of the format is a.{PARAM} which has a parameter named PARAM. If the lookup function has PARAM->b then the result will be a.b. If a value for a parameter is null (indicates not found) an exception is thrown.
      Parameters:
      key - to be interpolated.
      lookup - function that may return null for a parameter.
      Returns:
      interpolated key with all parameters replaced.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the lookup function does not have a value for a parameter.
